scope: Probe B domain phase T1: a transport per context (docs/plans/delegation-threads.md, Q2 first part), with the Probe A, signal-contract and application-gate regressions

platform.monitor: capstone-sbi monitor/context-slots dd812db (collects revocation nodes before a loan), in caplifive-opensbi wrapper/context-slots 3021c05 (caplifive-buildroot components/opensbi at cffac39)
platform.module_source: caplifive-buildroot modcapstone/context-slots, driver unchanged since e3a43d4
platform.kernel: /tmp/capstone/delegation-binfmt-linux Image, as in the earlier records

images_note: perl.dom and mruby.dom relinked on this runtime (ports/common/application/build.py, level0 heap, arena 64 MiB, heap log 26) from the objects /tmp/capstone/signals/perl5 and mruby4 were linked from, libc from /tmp/capstone/libc-rounds; the manifests say runtime_dirty because they were linked from the working tree that is this commit

thread_probe_measurements.many-rounds: thread-probe many-rounds: 100000 rounds in 9113 ms; 10000-round blocks 909 to 916 ms
thread_probe_measurements.signal-first-only: thread-probe signal-first-only: 20 handlers in the first context, 0 in the other

regression.context_probe: 35/35 standard modes PASS (two-steppers under the one-stepper contract); explicit modes in boots of their own on the same launcher: aba (A7, CAPSTONE_TEST_NODE_QUERY=1) PASS, gen-exhaust and gen-launch (A9, generation-preset firmware 759e8509) PASS, ctl-wfi PASS
regression.aba: context-probe aba: A node 78 base 0xc02bf000; 130381 burns; handle 78, area 78, new seal node 78 base 0xc02bf000; ids 0x100000001, 0x100000002; first step kind 0 cause 0 pc 0 result 0x4558495445444558 value 1005
regression.native: ctest in the native build of runtime/exec: 38/38 PASS, including application-image (contexts limit, page-sized exchange, the descriptor without contexts rejected) and delegate-service (a further context's host: own exchange, the owner's children and spawner, signal requests ENOSYS; every context request reaches the hook). The further-context refusal was shown to fire by removing it: delegate-service-test failed at the ENOSYS assertion.

findings.revocation_nodes: Every STEP that starts a call takes a revocation node for the descriptor loan; nothing collected them unless supervised code ran short itself. On the previous monitor (c0dbd04, firmware 8ceee8ebebb0d7ec505461b6d27d9f7471f3f5d0c78030fc1d6762436eb0bb26) thread-probe many-rounds (100000 sched_yield rounds, one context) halted the monitor: 'domain halted by capability fault: cause = 30, pc = 0x80021232' (mrev in loan_begin); so did context-probe two-steppers. With dd812db the same 100000 rounds pass.
findings.region_bounds: The runtime had sized the exchange region by the region capability's bounds, which can be larger than requested when the driver reuses a cached block. After thread-probe and context-probe (CONTEXTS 7) had run, signal-contract retry-partial got EFAULT: the launcher refused write(7, 0x10, 0x7fff0) against exchange_bytes 0x40000. Transports are now cut by the image's declared sizes; retry-partial passes after the same sequence.
findings.two_steppers: With a transport per context a THREAD context has one stepper; the application's STEP is refused with EINVAL (it would hand the context's request to the wrong thread). The mode now checks the refusal.

method: Guest runs through capstone_vm with the pinned files above: run-threads.py (thread-probe.dom), run-context.py, run-signals.py and run.py in one boot; A7, A9 and ctl-wfi in boots of their own. The pre-fix evidence came from the same probes on firmware 8ceee8eb (monitor c0dbd04) and on a runtime that still sized its exchange region by capability bounds.

review.what: An independent review of the T1 change (2026-09-30) found five defects. Three are fixed and covered by thread-probe modes that failed before the fix and pass after it (same firmware; launcher 66614e27 and the runtime before the fix); one is fixed by review only; one is left for Q6.
review.signal-first-only: A further context ran one of the first context's pending signal events (its round's dl_settle delivered from the process-wide list), after which the signal stayed blocked: before, '4 handlers in the first context, 1 in the other'; after, 20 and 0. Only a context with a handover block now takes, delivers or changes signal state.
review.exec-child: Exec in place from a further context started the new image with every signal blocked: before, the exec'd program read 'SigBlk:\tfffffffe7ffbfeff'; after, 0000000000000000 (the thread takes the application's logical mask just before execve).
review.sigpipe-child: SIGPIPE from a write in a further context stayed pending on its fully blocked thread and the process lived on (write -1, errno 32); now the thread forwards a pending SIGPIPE or SIGXFSZ to the process, which died by signal 13. sigpipe-ignored checks EPIPE under SIG_IGN.
review.exit_fault_exec: Exit, fault and exec in place now take one lock: an end that has begun wins, a failed exec gives the lock back (by review, no probe).
review.spawn_block: posix_spawn and execve pack into one static 64 KiB block in the domain; two contexts spawning at once would mix requests. Left for Q6 with malloc and stdio, which a further context also still runs without locks.
